summary: Pacific County, WA DNR live-in tower built 1962 on the Willapa-Columbia divide, named for Karl O. Lawrence; closed 1975; tower gone, footings remain.

facts.design: 20-foot wooden DNR live-in tower built by the DNR carpentry crew; a cabin stood at the spot in the 1940s before it
facts.status_note: The tower is gone. A 2021 photo caption on WillhiteWeb shows a communication building at the summit, and other captions show footings.
facts.agency: Washington Division of Forestry/DNR (Washington Department of Natural Resources)

access.note: WillhiteWeb says good gravel leads to a gate and an access permit is needed. Without a vehicle permit the bike ride is about 8.5 miles each way.

visit.trail_note: Routes are logging roads with many splits; active logging is a potential problem. No tower remains to climb, and the gate is the main limit.

events.note: DNR carpentry crew built a 20-foot wooden live-in tower; it replaced the Hull lookout on a nearby ridge
Firelookout lists Helen McGarity as known lookout personnel in 1962
Newspaper, June 1968: Karin Johnson of Willapa to be on duty; only one county lookout in service that year
WillhiteWeb says closed in 1975; a June 1977 newspaper says it had closed two years earlier
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register on January 17, 2012

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts places the old Hull lookout on the next ridge north; WillhiteWeb places it on the next ridge south. The story does not give a direction.
WillhiteWeb gives 1975 as the closing year. A June 1977 newspaper, quoted by Forest Lookouts, says the lookout had closed two years before that report, which fits 1975.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' is supported by the Register ('now gone'). No source gives the year the tower came down, so no removal event is recorded. Photo captions on WillhiteWeb (footings, communication building, February 2021) are the only description of the site today; they are not dated after 2021. Hull ridge direction conflicts (north per Forest Lookouts, south per WillhiteWeb). Helen McGarity (1962) comes only from the Firelookout personnel line. Access permit issuer is not named in any source read. The 'Removed' label on the Forest Lookouts page was not used. WillhiteWeb photos are credited to Klenke; license unknown, so none added to photos. Brief coordinates were not checked against any source. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the nine-lookouts and $8,000 figures are in Forest Lookouts' transcription of the DNR 3rd Biennial Report; the evidence now quotes that passage in full. The dedication date comes from the 6 Sept 1962 item quoted on Forest Lookouts.
